-- n_v17.haro -- N, the alphabet's sixth letter: the NATURAL. DRAWN from Ringua's Phase 1.5 study
-- (haro/study/phase15/STUDY.md), in the declaring altitude Haro already has: nothing here is new
-- meta-vocabulary but one (UNDERSTAND, at the end), so the meta-court accepts it and the forge emits a court that CHECKS sentences of
-- N. The dynamic half -- the `tokens`, `understand`, `ask`, `vocabulary` and `examples` verbs and the fourteen
-- rules of v17/GRAMMAR.md section 4b -- is what the one meta-clause, UNDERSTAND (the seventeenth rung), makes
-- the forge emit. Every kind and every seat below traces to a finding of the study (K1-K10).
--
-- N ASKS; IT NEVER DECLARES (06-ALPHABET, ratified 2026-09-27). A sentence of N declares tongues, meanings,
-- aliases, surfaces, frames, steps and examples -- how a human language reaches closed questions of a
-- declared world -- and never the world (Z declares it), the facts (the knowledge tier holds them) or a rule
-- (W constrains). A question is understood by exact shape against a frame or refused by name; nothing the
-- question says is evaluated, and a name in a question is never passed on: it is resolved through a surface
-- or refused. The reserved second half -- N may DRAFT, as a proposal the court judges and a human ratifies --
-- is not drawn from the study and is named in v17/GRAMMAR.md, not here.

DEFINE LANGUAGE n AS (
  VERSION "0.17",
  GRAMMAR "0.17",
  COURT "haro/study/phase15/fixtures/questions.json",
  EXTENSION ".n"
) RATIONALE "A human language over a declared world, closed: a question is one of the shapes a sentence declares, in any of the tongues it declares, compiled to a query a surface's own court judges -- or it is refused, by name, in the tongue it was asked in"

-- ---- the menus ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFINE MENU slots AS (
  WORDS [none, number, entity],
  MESSAGE "SLOT is none, number or entity, not '{value}': a meaning carries no value, a number the question wrote in digits, or an entity a surface knows by name",
  CODE "PARSE"
) RATIONALE "What a meaning captures from the question. There is no 'text' slot: a free string is the one thing a question may not carry into a query (E4, G3)"

DEFINE MENU surface_kinds AS (
  WORDS [query, pattern],
  MESSAGE "KIND is query or pattern, not '{value}'",
  CODE "PARSE"
) RATIONALE "The two closed query forms the study measured: a text question in a query grammar (ZQL), and a triple pattern (the knowledge graph)"

DEFINE MENU spellings AS (
  WORDS [as_is, upper_first],
  MESSAGE "a spelling is as_is or upper_first, not '{value}'",
  CODE "PARSE"
) RATIONALE "How a surface spells an entity the world knows by id: the graph says moussa and the ledger says Moussa (E1e). A declared convention, not an identity mechanism -- K2's typed field is the kit's"

DEFINE MENU refusal_kinds AS (
  WORDS [character, word, shape, ambiguous, surface],
  MESSAGE "a refusal is a character, a word, a shape, an ambiguity or a surface's refusal, not '{value}'",
  CODE "PARSE"
) RATIONALE "Every way a question ends without an answer, each said in the tongue it was asked in (K8): a character the gate refuses, a word the vocabulary lacks (a name the world does not know is such a word: Mallory, N04), a shape no frame has, an answer that is several entities where a plan needs one, a surface that refused the compiled query. Five kinds, five codes: N_CHARACTER, N_WORD, N_SHAPE, N_AMBIGUOUS, N_SURFACE"

DEFINE MENU digit_sets AS (
  WORDS [ascii],
  MESSAGE "DIGITS is ascii, the one numeric sublanguage the study measured, not '{value}'",
  CODE "PARSE"
) RATIONALE "K9: a numeric sublanguage per tongue. Today digits only -- a decimal, a sign, a spelled number and Arabic-Indic digits are all refused (N08-N10, N13); the menu is where they would be added"

-- ---- the forms ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFINE FORM word AS (
  SEATS [name: name]
) RATIONALE "One name"

DEFINE FORM in_tongue AS (
  SEATS [tongue: tongue, text: text]
) RATIONALE "A text in one tongue. The tongue-keyed pair list is how a language is a COLUMN of a declaration and not a copy of it (E3b against E2c): add a tongue by adding a pair, never code"

DEFINE FORM refusal_text AS (
  SEATS [kind: refusal_kinds, text: text]
) RATIONALE "What a tongue says for one kind of refusal; {what} is the thing not understood"

DEFINE FORM spelling AS (
  SEATS [entity: name, how: spellings]
) RATIONALE "How one entity kind is spelled in the queries of a surface"

-- ---- the kinds ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFINE DECLARATION tongue AS (
  VERB "TONGUE",
  SEATS [code: text, ignores: text, allows: text?, digits: digit_sets?, names: spellings?, joins: text?, refuses: [refusal_text]],
  MESSAGES [
    code: "TONGUE {name} needs its CODE, the language's own short name (en, fr)",
    ignores: "TONGUE {name} needs IGNORES, the words a question may carry that mean nothing (the, a, de, le); an empty text if none"
  ],
  CODES [code: "TONGUE_INCOMPLETE", ignores: "TONGUE_INCOMPLETE"]
) RATIONALE "A human language the surface speaks: its code, the words it lets pass, the punctuation it allows beyond letters, digits and the space (and only from the court's safe set: a tongue cannot widen the gate -- K4), how it writes a name in an answer and the word that joins the last of several (a tongue's own conventions; found by building the court, the drawing had put French's `et` in code), and how it refuses (K8)"

DEFINE DECLARATION meaning AS (
  VERB "MEANING",
  SEATS [slot: slots, of: name?, from: surface?, words: [in_tongue]?],
  MESSAGES [
    slot: "MEANING {name} needs a SLOT: none, number or entity",
    from: "MEANING {name} draws its entities from '{value}', which is not a declared surface"
  ],
  CODES [slot: "MEANING_INCOMPLETE", from: "DANGLING_SURFACE"]
) RATIONALE "One thing a question can mean, once, under every tongue: its words per tongue (a column each), what it captures (nothing, digits, or an entity of a kind OF a surface FROM which the words are generated -- a name is a word because the world has it, never because the question wrote it)"

DEFINE DECLARATION alias AS (
  VERB "ALIAS",
  SEATS [meaning: meaning, entity: text, words: [in_tongue]],
  MESSAGES [meaning: "ALIAS {name} is of '{value}', which is not a declared meaning"],
  CODES [meaning: "DANGLING_MEANING"]
) RATIONALE "Words for one entity of the world, per tongue: the treasurer is trésorier in French and treasurer in English, and both are the one entity the surface knows"

DEFINE DECLARATION surface AS (
  VERB "SURFACE",
  SEATS [kind: surface_kinds, grammar: text, court: text, world: text?, entities: [word]?, spells: [spelling]?, tells: [tongue]?],
  MESSAGES [
    kind: "SURFACE {name} needs a KIND: query or pattern",
    grammar: "SURFACE {name} needs its GRAMMAR, the closed query grammar its court judges",
    court: "SURFACE {name} needs its COURT, the court that judges and runs a query: a surface is a protocol, never a library",
    tells: "SURFACE {name} tells in '{value}', which is not a declared tongue"
  ],
  CODES [kind: "SURFACE_INCOMPLETE", grammar: "SURFACE_INCOMPLETE", court: "SURFACE_INCOMPLETE", tells: "DANGLING_TONGUE"]
) RATIONALE "A closed place a question can end: the grammar its queries are written in, the court that judges them (`surface-check`) and runs them (`surface-run`), the versioned world it reads, the entity kinds it can enumerate, how it spells them, and the tongues it can tell an answer in. N knows no ZQL and no stzKnowledgeGraph -- only this protocol (D-N7)"

DEFINE DECLARATION step AS (
  VERB "STEP",
  SEATS [target: surface, query: text, binds: name?],
  MESSAGES [target: "STEP {name} is aimed at '{value}', which is not a declared surface"],
  CODES [target: "DANGLING_SURFACE"]
) RATIONALE "One query of a plan, to one surface. BINDS names the slot the answer fills for the steps after it, and an answer that is not exactly one entity stops the plan (K6)"

DEFINE DECLARATION frame AS (
  VERB "FRAME",
  SEATS [shape: [meaning], target: surface?, query: text?, steps: [step]?, answers: [in_tongue]?, empty: [in_tongue]?],
  MESSAGES [
    shape: "FRAME {name} has '{value}' in its SHAPE, which is not a declared meaning",
    target: "FRAME {name} is aimed at '{value}', which is not a declared surface",
    steps: "FRAME {name} steps to '{value}', which is not a declared step"
  ],
  CODES [shape: "DANGLING_MEANING", target: "DANGLING_SURFACE", steps: "DANGLING_STEP"]
) RATIONALE "One shape of question, exact: the meanings it is made of, in order, and the closed query it compiles to -- one TARGET and QUERY, or a plan of STEPS. {slot} placeholders are the shape's own slots. A question that fits no frame is refused; nothing is guessed (D-N5)"

DEFINE DECLARATION example AS (
  VERB "EXAMPLE",
  SEATS [means: frame, asking: [in_tongue]],
  MESSAGES [means: "EXAMPLE {name} means '{value}', which is not a declared frame"],
  CODES [means: "DANGLING_FRAME"]
) RATIONALE "The sentence's own conformance (K10): each text, in each tongue, must be understood as this frame, and every tongue must compile to the SAME closed query -- the multilingual invariance (G2) as a law of the sentence"

DEFINE DECLARATION counterexample AS (
  VERB "COUNTEREXAMPLE",
  SEATS [asking: [in_tongue], refused: refusal_kinds]
) RATIONALE "What the sentence promises NOT to understand: each text must be refused, as this kind. Precision, not recall, is what N measures (STUDY section 7)"

-- ---- the refusals of a sentence ------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFINE REFUSAL unknown_declaration AS (
  MESSAGE "A sentence of N declares TONGUE, MEANING, ALIAS, SURFACE, FRAME, STEP, EXAMPLE and COUNTEREXAMPLE, and nothing else. N asks; it never declares the world, the facts or a rule."
) RATIONALE "Rule 1 of Ringua, as a refusal: natural language asks, it never declares"

DEFINE REFUSAL dangling_reference AS (
  MESSAGE "This name resolves to nothing the sentence declares: a tongue, a meaning, a surface, a step or a frame."
) RATIONALE "Every word of a tongue is a word of a declared meaning, every shape a list of declared meanings, every target a declared surface"

-- ---- the meta-clause: what the forge emits the dynamic verbs for ---------------------------------------

DEFINE UNDERSTAND n AS (
  TONGUE [tongue], MEANING [meaning], ALIAS [alias], SURFACE [surface],
  STEP [step], FRAME [frame], EXAMPLE [example], COUNTEREXAMPLE [counterexample]
) RATIONALE "Which declarations of this language play the eight roles of a human language over a declared world; the forge emits tokens, understand, ask, vocabulary and examples for them, and the fourteen rules of GRAMMAR section 4b as the court's own"
